title: A kernel path that should not have been that hot
dek: Someone read the scheduler. Then they could not unread it.
description: A deep dive into an unexpected cost in a kernel hot path, with patches and measurements from the authors.

analysis.why_you_should_care: Performance work at this layer changes how you see every userspace benchmark.
analysis.what_happened: An engineer traced an unexpected kernel cost, explained the path, and proposed a change. Demo reconstruction.
analysis.how_it_works: A seemingly innocent syscall or scheduling decision takes a lock or walks a structure too often. The fix is usually a data-structure change, not a compiler flag.
analysis.under_the_hood: Follow the tracepoints. If you cannot name the lock, you are still in the blog post.
analysis.why_they_built_it: The numbers were embarrassing and the cause was hiding in a file everyone thought was finished.
analysis.what_was_difficult: Proving the fix does not invert some other workload.
analysis.performance: Use only author-published traces. This demo does not invent counters.
analysis.trade_offs: Throughput versus latency, fairness versus cache warmth.
analysis.what_is_surprising: The hot path was not where the comments said it would be.
analysis.quick_read: A kernel hot path, explained like a crime scene.
